verdict.rationale: Visa's own docs address chargebacks only partly. They say commerce signals capturing the user's original instruction and each authorized purchase "allow for the quick resolution of most disputes". TAP tells merchants to decline when credential hashes don't match, and says that after verifying a payment IOU they can expect funds at settlement. None of this states who bears fraud or chargeback liability for agent-initiated transactions. missing for 10: explicit liability-shift/allocation rules, documented chargeback reason codes or dispute process for agent transactions, merchant-facing fraud liability terms, independent corroboration.

support.subject: As a merchant, the fraud, liability, and chargeback rules for agent-initiated transactions are documented so I know who bears the risk

citations.quote: Collection of commerce signals that will provide the user’s original instruction and the details of each authorized purchase allow for the quick resolution of most disputes
If the hashes do not match, the information being key entered is most likely fraudulent and the Merchant should decline the transaction.
the Merchant can grant access with the expectation that the funds will be available when settlement occurs.
